implement: legion-worker: the push, the proof object, the pull-request body, the findings route and the production check after the close; this issue's code and handoffs share one branch on sjawhar/legion, and the first push is also the permission proof the replaced issue died on.
dispatch-first: search before any finding, ask or message; this issue already has three siblings in the same lane (INFRA-490, INFRA-524, INFRA-756) and a replaced issue whose record carries the work.
dispatch: the issue's comments and artifacts, and the rule that a Legion role never writes its own issue's lifecycle status.
asd-ste100: the pull-request body and every message a person reads; the body carries measured tables a reviewer must read once.
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the listener test helpers and the new ci.yaml jobs before the body is written.
test: legion-worker: the tester's proof object, and the rule to re-run the implementer's named commands at the head that merges; here that is about two hours of pod loops plus three CI runs read first-hand.
dispatch: read the issue and its comments before the loops, since the architect's decisions DB-1 to DB-5 can change what the loops must show.
review: legion-worker: the merge gate, review threads, and the proof rules the review checks; this change's evidence is measurement tables, so each figure must name the run it came from.
asd-ste100: the body and any text a person reads.

findings.answer: Plan departure D-9 and architect decision DB-1: every race job carries -timeout 30m and the bar is 1080 s, so both readings of the criterion are the same number. The plan proceeds on that recommendation and names the one line of INFRA-756's acceptance it changes.

findings.answer: Architect decision DB-4 and plan section 8: tasks A, B and the four non-docs jobs touch no line INFRA-756 touches and land first; only C3's shard of docs needs that job to exist, and if it is absent the implementer reports to the architect rather than taking docs into this pull request, because INFRA-756's acceptance 4 is a scope boundary. (The gap analysis reported INFRA-756 as blocked_by INFRA-605; a fresh read of INFRA-756 shows only child_of INFRA-490, so it is not blocked.)

findings.finding: The spec's headroom numbers are stale, and the measurement the shard count needs does not exist; the lane's second step has never printed a package line on main.
findings.answer: Plan departure D-2 carries the fresh reading from run 40877712458 job 123461966609 for all seven packages, and states that the second step is unmeasured. Task C2 takes the first isolated measurement from three runs of this pull request, and C3's shard count is the smallest N whose slowest shard is at or under 1080 s on all three. A package that grows again is re-measured and gains a shard, never a longer -timeout.

findings.finding: "The same set of tests run in total" has no machine check on the test-name route, and the complementary regex pair proposed is not complete: [^A-M] matches one character, a function named exactly Test lands in neither shard, Example and Fuzz are dropped, and 308 of 625 docs tests begin TestA so the split is 49/51 at best.
findings.answer: Plan section 6, C3: the -run route is rejected for exactly these reasons and the reasons are written into the plan. The split is by complementary build constraints, with an in-package test asserting that every file declaring a top-level Test, Benchmark, Example or Fuzz carries exactly one of the two constraints and a helper-only file carries neither, modelled on pgmigratetest.CheckEmbedsEveryFile, plus the untagged go test -list union check in the body.

findings.finding: -run shards cost two pinned gate entries and one filter per shard, and per-package filters cannot narrow api or store, which deletes DA-2's saving for those jobs.
findings.answer: Plan section 6, C1: the envoy-go-race-api and envoy-go-race-bus filters keep packages/envoy/** because api's lock_level_test.go and store's search_text_test.go walk every source file under packages/envoy; the other jobs' filters are computed by the guide's go list -deps -test method, and that is where DA-2's saving comes from. The plan says so rather than claiming a saving it cannot get.

findings.finding: Acceptance 3's seven-day half belongs to an issue (INFRA-524) whose only record of the scan names the replaced issue INFRA-747 and a pull request that does not exist.
findings.answer: Plan departure D-8 and architect decision DB-3: acceptance 3 is read as ci-ok green on the merging head plus the production check's one scan recorded on the pull request, and the architect moves the day-7 reading onto INFRA-524 under this issue's key. The scan command and the rule that a window with no run of each job proves nothing are in plan section 9.

Plan section 10 names the fresh red by its real name, TestADrainEndsTheKVWatchersBeforeTheConnection, and the issue that owns the bus flakes, dispatch://INFRA-750, with its two pull requests in flight.

findings.finding: DA-2's two numbers are undefined for jobs with no history, and its "up to half of today's single job" allowance was never priced.
findings.answer: Architect decision DB-2 and plan section 6, C8: isolating packages removes contention, so a full selection's summed runner minutes necessarily rise by roughly the parallelism factor (one 31.6-minute job to about 95-125 minutes plus per-job setup), which is three to fourfold, not a half. The plan prices both numbers by the parent's method (ceil((completed_at - started_at)/60) per job; the replay recipe of the pr2316 solutions page, costing each new job at this pull request's own measured minutes), states they are runner-capacity minutes and not money, and takes the arithmetic to the architect before the lane change lands, as DA-2 itself requires.

findings.finding: Flake B has no decided reproduction device, and nothing committed would hold the fix in place; the existing timeOutRoleClaimScan times the scan out permanently, so the fixed test cannot pass under it.
findings.answer: Plan section 5, task B2: a committed regression test inside package main that installs a kvwatchtest.TimingOutFirst-backed role watcher through the reflect seam the package already uses, so the first scan alone stalls while WithRescan lets a later one complete. It fails on main's code and passes at the head. The uncommitted environment-variable delay stays the device for the narrow-window readings only, and its diff is quoted in the body.

The product half is architect decision DB-5, with the recommendation that it stays out of this issue because the refusal is correct in kind and already names its cause, and changing the prefix changes a wire-visible body.

findings.finding: The carried work exists only as an artifact, task C1 was never written, and the previous pod could not push to sjawhar/legion at all.

findings.answer: Plan section 6, C7: the pull request updates packages/envoy/AGENTS.md (both sentences, the job count dropped rather than restated), docs/testing.md and the INFRA-141 solutions page, and the body answers in one sentence why the shards owe no canary and injected-race proof under the INFRA-271 page: shard membership changes no test and adds no goroutine, and the union check proves the same set runs.

specDepartures.spec: The spec says TestThreeBrowsersAndTheAPIEditOneRoomAtOnce "refuses to start with under 90 s left, so it silently stops running", and asks that a test which skips because too little time is left fails instead of passing silently.
specDepartures.plan: No such skip exists, so the plan treats the bullet as already true, proves it with a negative control (go test -race -timeout 2m over that test must fail by name), and carries the real constraint forward as a shard sizing rule: no shard may leave overlapping 90 s or less, or roomWait 30 s or less, of its own -timeout.
specDepartures.evidence: overlapping (internal/dispatch/docs/live_read_race_test.go, overlapMargin 90 s), roomWait (settlement_credit_test.go, roomWaitMargin 30 s) and throughputWait (internal/dispatch/api/live_socket_test.go) each call t.Fatalf. A scout enumerated every t.Skip and b.Skip in the packages/envoy Go tree: none reads a deadline or a clock. sjawhar/legion job 123503246603 shows the docs package FAILing at 1801.1 s with 69 tests refused by the guard.

outcome.acceptance: The "Also delivered" bullet asking that a deadline-conditioned skip fail becomes a negative control proving the guards already fail, plus the shard sizing rule.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's design holds only internal/dispatch/docs to the 60% bar: "the race lane splits that package into shards ... so the slowest shard uses at most 60% of its timeout".
specDepartures.plan: Every job of the race lane is held to the bar, and the lane's second step is measured for the first time.
specDepartures.evidence: Run 40877712458, job 123461966609, main 14d907b6: docs 1772.969 s, pmdoc 1563.552 s, api 1099.487 s, bus 315.651 s (FAIL), store 277.864 s, delivery 93.562 s. Against 1080 s that is 164%, 145% and 102% for the first three. The job ended red on internal/bus, so ./cmd/listener/ ./internal/store/ ./internal/kvwatch/... printed no package line and has never been measured on main.

outcome.scope: The lane change covers every race job, not the docs package alone; the architect settled this as DA-1 on the replaced issue.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's design is to split the docs package into shards.
specDepartures.plan: Each package group gets a job of its own first, the isolated figure is measured on three runs of this pull request, and a package is split only where its own figure is still over 1080 s.
specDepartures.evidence: Every figure above was taken with six race binaries contending for four vCPUs in one go test invocation, so none says what a package costs on a runner of its own. Sharding internal/dispatch/docs by build constraint touches 69 of its 72 test files, and sixteen open pull requests sit in that directory today (#2497, #2496, #2485, #2483, #2480, #2468, #2463, #2445, #2444, #2433, #2414, #2395, #2394, #2392, #2391, #2387).

outcome.scope: Shards are conditional on a measurement rather than given; if isolation alone meets the bar, no package is split and the architect decides whether the spec changes.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1 asks for a reproduction that fails on main's code, "a loop under load, as docs/solutions/testing/widen-the-contender-count-before-calling-a-race-unreproducible.md describes".
specDepartures.plan: Flake A keeps the load loop. Flake B's reproduction is a forced one: a device that holds the role-claim watcher's first scan back, with the unforced loop recorded beside it as the control. The plan also commits a regression test built on kvwatchtest.TimingOutFirst and the reflect seam the package already uses, which fails on main's code and passes at the head.
specDepartures.evidence: INFRA-747's implementer ran the load loop against the listener test: 0 failures in 228 iterations. With the watcher's first scan held back it fails five of five at 50 ms and 20 ms, four of five at 10 ms, none at 5 ms and below. The margin the test leaves the watcher is between 5 ms and 10 ms, which a shared GitHub runner reaches and a quiet pod does not.

outcome.acceptance: For flake B, "a loop under load that fails on main's code" becomes a forced reproduction plus a committed regression test, with the load loop recorded as the control that shows it proves nothing here.
